hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, from an unidentified man, from Ikrimah, who was asked about making up Ramadan: together or separately? He said: Whichever of that he wishes. Allah said: 'Two months consecutively' (Quran 4:92), and if He had wished, He would have said: Whoever makes up Ramadan, then together. But He did not say anything about it, and the righteous people did not forbid it, so they follow what is permissible

hadiths.arabicText: عَنِ /94 ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ /94 ، /27 عَنْ /26 عَطَاءٍ /26 ، قَالَ : قُلْتُ أَرَأَيْتَ /20 إِنْ كَانَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَيَّامِ رَمَضَانَ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', he said: I said, what do you think if a man has days from Ramadan to make up, and he wakes up one day without intending to fast, then it occurs to him after he has awakened - can he count it as making up Ramadan even though he did not intend it before Fajr? He said: Let him fast it and count it as making up Ramadan

hadiths.english_translation: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah and Asim, that they both heard Ikrimah say: Ibn Abbas said: Umar ibn al-Khattab called the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ and asked them about Laylat al-Qadr. They all agreed that it is in the last ten nights. Ibn Abbas said: I said to Umar: I know, or I think I know, which night it is. Umar said: Which night is it? I said: The seventh that passes, or the seventh that remains of the last ten nights. Umar said: From where did you know that? He said: Allah created seven heavens, seven earths, seven days, and the age revolves in sevens, Allah created man from seven, he eats from seven, prostrates on seven, Tawaf of the House is seven, and stoning the Jamarat is seven - for things he mentioned. Umar said: You have understood something we did not understand
